children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower on Wednesday, with attention turning toward U.S. Department of Agriculture data to be released on Friday, which will offer a gauge of weather damage to Midwest crops.
The USDA's supply-and-demand forecasts are awaited as an indicator of the extent to which hot, dry spells this summer hurt U.S. Midwest crops such as soybeans.
In a Reuters poll, analysts on average predict that the USDA will estimate corn yield for the month at 178.2 bushels per acre.

The weather pattern in the U.S. Midwest is expected to be mildly wetter in the coming weeks, but only limited delays to the soybean harvest are predicted, according to forecaster Commodity Weather Group.
Brazil's corn exports are seen reaching 5.2 million tons in September vs. 6.98 millions tons in the same period last year, according to grain exporters union ANEC.
Exporters sold 182,880 metric tons of corn to Mexico for 2026/2027 delivery, according to the USDA.
On Tuesday, the USDA estimated that 56% of the corn crop was in good-to-excellent condition, down 1 percentage point from the previous week but in line with average analyst expectations.
settled 5-3/4 cents lower to $5.27-3/4 per bushel.
